svg.title: NeuroMechFly tethered in the air, its front legs moved by the leg motor neurons of brainfly's nerve cord with DNg100 driven: the left front leg swings at the rhythm's 12 Hz, but its foot runs up and down a line instead of stepping
svg.text: The nerve cord's rhythm moves the front legs
NeuroMechFly tethered in the air, its front legs pulled by the leg motor neurons of brainfly's nerve cord with the right DNg100 driven; played 25× slower
Thin red line: the left foot's path over these three cycles. Dashed: the foot in a fly's recorded step, around the same thorax.
The left leg swings at its motor neurons' 12.0 Hz
so do 8 more replicates, at 10.9–15.4 Hz
ThC pitch 58°, CTr pitch 32° peak to peak
one gain, fitted to a fly step's 32° and 58°
the motor neurons' rates have a large steady part
The foot runs along a line: loop index 0.10
a fly's step 0.52; the 8 replicates at most 0.10
Swing and stance muscles fire together
promotors, Tr flexors 14° apart: both lift the foot
No tibia or tarsus motor neuron is active
each DNg100 drives the opposite leg alone
No drive: no motor neuron fires; legs still
Rewired: 100–108 motor neurons on, no rhythm;
motors at their cap, legs held at extremes
Standing: the foot is off the ground 98% of the time
The left leg's motor neurons and joints
